title: Pooled versus arm-separate matching in anchored MAIC
question: Arm-separate matching weights each individual-data arm to the corresponding aggregate arm; pooled matching uses one weight function. When does each give a biased anchored comparison, and is the bias of arm-separate matching the product of unmatched prognostic strength and aggregate arm imbalance, as the design claims?
design: Continuous outcome, one matched and one unmatched prognostic covariate, 96 cells crossing an imposed aggregate-trial imbalance, the unmatched covariate's prognostic strength, the covariate correlation in each trial, and shared effect modification. Unadjusted, pooled, arm-separate and two-stage MAIC. 1000 replicates per cell.
